sources: The **National Report** (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/1) was not yet available at the time of assessment.
meta.headline: **No relevant action (C)** is the dominant outcome, with a thin evidence base on the State's own account because its National Report was not yet available. **Partial implementation (B)** appears where the documents record concrete measures: the 2023 amendment of the Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act and a 2021-2025 action plan, a National Task Force on Gender-Based Violence (2024), a National Child Protection Policy, the national climate and adaptation framework, expanded social protection after the 2021 volcanic eruption and the new Belle Isle detention facility. **No relevant action (C)** persists on ICPPED, OP-CAT and the other unratified protocols, a comprehensive anti-discrimination law, decriminalisation of same-sex conduct (sections 146 and 148), the death penalty (a de facto moratorium since 1995 but one person on death row), the minimum age of marriage, a national human rights institution, the pending Sexual Offences Bill and criminalisation of marital rape and sexual harassment, and corporal punishment. Many recommendations have no information in the documents (**D**).
meta.note: No national report was available for this review when the assessment was made, so more recommendations are graded D (no information).

themes.theme: Ratification of & accession to international instruments

blocks.summary: Ratify outstanding treaties and optional protocols
blocks.rationale: The country has ratified the major core treaties but not ICPPED, the Second Optional Protocol to the ICCPR, OP-CAT, OP-CEDAW, OP-ICESCR, OP-CRC on communications or the American Convention; no ratification in the review period is reported.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 3 — United Nations subregional team in Barbados: "had not ratified the Second Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights"

recommendations.text: Adopt a formal moratorium on the death penalty with a view to ratifying the Second Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, aiming at the abolition of the death penalty
Abolish the death penalty
Implement an official moratorium on the death penalty with a view to abolishing it
Establish an official moratorium on the death penalty, and conduct appropriate awareness-raising measures to mobilize public opinion for the abolition of the death penalty
Establish an official moratorium on executions, and abolish the death penalty in national legislation

blocks.summary: Continue the de facto moratorium

evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 11 — JS4: "had observed a de facto moratorium on executions since 1995"

recommendations.text: Continue the moratorium on the death penalty

themes.theme: Cooperation with human rights mechanisms & requests for technical assistance

blocks.summary: Seek OHCHR and regional technical assistance
blocks.rationale: The country sought technical assistance to strengthen reporting and implementation, with UN-supported capacity-building since 2021, and an OHCHR Regional Office for the Caribbean was established in 2024.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 6 — United Nations subregional team: "had sought technical assistance to strengthen national reporting capacity and the implementation of treaty body recommendations"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 9 — OHCHR: "In 2024, the OHCHR Regional Office for the Caribbean was established"

recommendations.text: Request technical support from the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights to advance in the ratification of the main international human rights instruments to which the country is not yet a party, as well as to ensure the alignment of its national legal system with the obligations arising from ratified human rights treaties
Engage with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights to seek assistance in the implementation of the core international human rights treaties
Seek technical assistance from the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights to meet international human rights obligations and to facilitate human rights training and education
Request technical assistance from regional and international agencies to conduct training and the collection and analysis of data to enable the systematic implementation of human rights commitments

themes.theme: Cooperation & Follow up with Special Procedures

blocks.summary: Standing invitation to special procedures

recommendations.text: Extend a standing invitation to special procedures of the Human Rights Council
Extend an open and standing invitation to all special procedure mandate holders
Consider extending a standing invitation to special procedure mandate holders
Consider extending a standing invitation to all special procedure mandate holders

blocks.summary: Bring legislation into line with international obligations

evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 10 — Special Rapporteur on environment: "economic, social, cultural and environmental rights were not guaranteed in the Constitution"

recommendations.text: Continue its efforts to bring its national legislative framework into line with the international human rights instruments it has ratified

blocks.summary: Establish a Paris-Principles national human rights institution
blocks.rationale: No independent institution exists and the feasibility study accepted in the previous cycle has not been carried out; the recommendation has been repeated in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 cycles.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 5 — JS5: "the State did not have an independent national human rights institution and had not conducted the feasibility study"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 11 — Special Rapporteur on environment: "a recommendation made during the 2011, 2016 and 2021 universal periodic review cycles"

recommendations.text: Establish and operationalize the national human rights institute in accordance with the Paris Principles, in consultation with stakeholders, in particular human rights organizations

Continue to take substantive measures to establish a national human rights institution and develop a national action plan of human rights for systematic and comprehensive actions for promotion and protection of human rights for all people in the country
Consider establishing an independent national human rights institution in accordance with the Paris Principles

Consider establishing an independent national human rights institution, with a broad mandate to protect human rights, with adequate human and financial resources, and in accordance with the Paris Principles
Advance the goal to establish a national human rights institution in accordance with the Paris Principles
Establish an independent national human rights institution, in accordance with the Paris Principles
Establish a national human rights institution in accordance with the Paris Principles
Establish a national human rights institution in accordance with the Paris Principles as a matter of priority
Continue its efforts to create a national human rights institution with a broad mandate to protect human rights and with sufficient financial and human resources for its implementation
Establish an independent national human rights institution compliant with the Paris Principles
Advance steps towards completion of feasibility studies related to the establishment of the national human rights institution
Continue its efforts to establish a national human rights institution that complies with the Paris Principles

blocks.summary: National mechanism for monitoring and reporting

evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 7 — JS1: "established the National Human Rights Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs"

recommendations.text: Establish a human rights institution to observe the national human rights situation and in pursuance of an improvement to follow-up on recommendations and implementation of international human rights treaties

blocks.summary: Adopt comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation
blocks.rationale: The Constitution covers only six grounds and no comprehensive anti-discrimination law has been adopted; consensual same-sex conduct remains criminalised under sections 146 and 148 of the Criminal Code.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 12 — United Nations subregional team: "the legal framework in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines still lacked explicit protections against discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and that no comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation had been adopted"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 52 — Three submissions: "consensual samesex conduct was criminalized under sections 146 and 148 of the Penal Code"

recommendations.text: Consider adopting legislation which provides full and effective protection against discrimination and prohibits direct, indirect and intersecting discrimination, including measures for its effective implementation, with a particular emphasis on discrimination on the grounds of gender, sexual orientation, and gender identity and expression
Take all steps necessary to end discrimination against and stigmatization of LGBTI+ persons, including by amending the Criminal Code to decriminalize consensual same-sex sexual activity
Decriminalize consensual adult same-sex relations and combat discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons

Decriminalize sexual relations between consenting adults of the same sex and undertake concrete measures to combat stigma and discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons

Reform laws under section 146 and 148 of the Criminal Code of 1988 related to discrimination and gender-based violence against women and LGBTQI+ persons, including by repealing provisions that may be used to criminalize consensual, same-sex sexual activity between adults, and establishing a law criminalizing domestic violence
Reaffirm its commitment to the principle of non-discrimination by encouraging the necessary debates for the prompt decriminalization of consensual sexual relations between adults of the same sex
Adopt national anti-discrimination legislation, in particular for the LGBTQI+ population, including decriminalization of consensual same-sex relations
Decriminalize same-sex conduct between consenting adults by amending section 146 and 148 of the Criminal Code
Decriminalize same-sex relations and remove the buggery laws with respect to sexual acts between consenting adults
Do not criminalize consensual sexual conduct between people of the same sex
Decriminalize consensual same-sex conduct, by abolishing section 148 of the Criminal Code

Decriminalize consensual homosexual relationships between adults and include legislation that prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
Prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, including by repealing all laws criminalizing sexual relations between consenting adults
Ensure that national anti-discrimination legislation provides for full and effective protection against discrimination in all spheres and prohibits direct, indirect and multiple discrimination

blocks.summary: Continue measures against discrimination

evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 12 — United Nations subregional team: "no comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation had been adopted"

blocks.summary: Awareness campaigns against discrimination
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Launch, in dialogue with civil society organizations, awareness campaigns aimed at addressing discriminatory gender norms and attitudes, including those that affect the enjoyment of human rights by women and girls and the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex population

blocks.summary: Anti-discrimination protection for people with HIV
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Further strengthen legislation to prohibit any form of discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity or social status and especially to prevent any form of discrimination and harassment against women by including domestic violence as a criminal offence in the Domestic Violence Act

blocks.summary: Human-rights-centred reform of law enforcement

blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Intensify efforts to guarantee freedom of association and assembly

themes.theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery

blocks.summary: Combat trafficking in persons
blocks.rationale: The Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act was amended in 2023 and a National Action Plan 2021-2025 adopted, but no victim has been identified since the last review and prosecutions are lacking.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 20 — ILO Committee of Experts: "had been amended in 2023 in regard to the penalties for offences"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 21 — United Nations subregional team: "had adopted a National Action Plan to Combat Trafficking in Persons, for 2021–2025"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 21 — ECLJ: "failure to identify a single victim of human trafficking since the last universal periodic review"

recommendations.text: Strengthen the measures implemented to combat human trafficking, reinforcing the effective application of the Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act, as well as its corresponding national plan
Further strengthen the provision of appropriate services to victims of trafficking, especially women and children, and facilitate their rehabilitation and social integration
Continue its efforts to implement the national action plan to combat human trafficking
Continue efforts aimed at strengthening the implementation of the national plan to combat trafficking

blocks.summary: Investigate and prosecute trafficking
blocks.rationale: There is a decade-long lack of prosecutions and the Anti-Trafficking Unit is underfunded.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 20 — ECLJ: "a decade-long lack of prosecutions and insufficient services for victims"

recommendations.text: Effectively investigate and prosecute cases of trafficking in persons

evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 20 — ECLJ: "in 2023 Saint Vincent and the Grenadines had amended the Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act to enact stricter penalties for individuals convicted of human trafficking"

blocks.summary: Legal protection of children from sale and sexual exploitation
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

blocks.summary: Retention of pregnant students and inclusive education

themes.theme: Right to an adequate standard of living

blocks.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment
blocks.rationale: The Education Act authorises corporal punishment in schools and it is lawful at home as 'reasonable punishment'.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 54 — UNESCO: "the Education Act of 2006 authorized the use of corporal punishment in schools"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 45 — CCI: "legally permitted under the concept of 'reasonable punishment'"

recommendations.text: Abolish corporal punishment by law and in practice, by enacting specific national legislation prohibiting corporal punishment in all environments
Implement measures to prohibit corporal punishment and promote a non-violent form of discipline

blocks.summary: Strengthen the national health system
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no specific information on measures on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Continue strengthening its national health system to protect the lives of its people, especially those most vulnerable to the COVID-19 pandemic
Address negative cultural attitudes by health workers against adolescent girls seeking contraceptive services, while respecting confidentiality and their right to privacy

blocks.summary: Criminalise marital rape, sexual harassment and domestic violence
blocks.rationale: The Sexual Offences Bill has been pending for over five years; the Employment Relations (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Bill is not adopted and domestic violence is treated as a civil matter.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 40 — JS1: "had not implemented the recommendations from the previous universal periodic review related to explicitly making marital rape a crime and enacting a sexual harassment bill"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 39 — JS1: "under the 2015 Domestic Violence Act, domestic violence was treated as a civil matter and not a crime"

recommendations.text: Continue its efforts to reform the sexual offences legislation

Redouble efforts to curb domestic and sexual violence and abuse, as well as consider enacting legislation criminalizing sexual harassment and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
Continue efforts to strengthen laws against sexual crimes and prohibit marital rape and sexual harassment in the Criminal Code

Implement legislation on sexual and gender-based violence, including marital rape and other forms of domestic violence and family violence; and ensure that victim-survivors can access justice, support mechanisms and necessary services
Redouble efforts to complete the enactment of the prevention of sexual harassment bill in Parliament
Include marital rape and sexual harassment as criminal offences under the Criminal Code
Include domestic violence as a criminal offence under the Domestic Violence Act

blocks.summary: Combat sexual and gender-based violence
blocks.rationale: A National Task Force on Gender-Based Violence was launched in 2024 and anti-violence campaigns run; however the Sexual Offences Bill has been pending for over five years and marital rape, sexual harassment and domestic violence are not criminal offences.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 51 — United Nations subregional team: "in 2024 the country had launched the National Task Force on Gender-Based Violence"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 40 — JS1: "had been working for over 5 years on a Sexual Offences Bill to update laws in relation to sexual offences under the Criminal Code, but that the bill was still pending"

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Ensure that all perpetrators of abuse towards women and girls are held to account, and implement capacity-building training for police officers and other law enforcement officials in gender-based violence and sexual abuse reporting
Ensure greater stakeholder involvement in the implementation of measures to combat gender-based violence
Redouble efforts to combat discrimination against women and reduce high rates of domestic violence, sexual violence and sexual abuse

Implement policy measures to eliminate discrimination against women with regard to preventing and punishing gender-based violence and promoting equal representation of women in political, social and economic spheres as well as leadership
Consider taking necessary measures to strengthen legislation against gender-based violence and sexual abuse
Continue to take all necessary measures to effectively combat domestic violence and provide a victim-based approach

blocks.summary: Establish facilities for victims of violence
blocks.rationale: Crisis housing exists but access is restricted to those with a court protection order, and victim support services lack resources.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 44 — ICAAD: "improve access to government-established crisis and emergency housing for gender-based violence and domestic violence victims by removing any requirement"

recommendations.text: Urgently create a safe and functional institution for victims of gender-based violence and sexual abuse and implement capacity-building training for police officers and other law enforcement officials in gender-based violence and sexual abuse reporting

Counter gender-based violence, including through the creation of an institution for victims of gender-based violence and sexual abuse, and by strengthening training for law enforcement personnel on gender-based violence and sexual abuse reporting
Establish facilities and institutions where victims of intimate partner violence, sexual violence and child sexual abuse can find a safe space in order to escape a vicious cycle of dependence

blocks.summary: Public awareness campaigns against gender-based violence
blocks.rationale: Gender Affairs ran anti-violence campaigns in schools, clinics and communities in 2024.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 42 — ICAAD: "Gender Affairs undertook antiviolence campaigns in schools, clinics and communities"

recommendations.text: Implement public awareness campaigns to end gender-based violence and violence against women and children

blocks.summary: Support and referral services for victims
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no specific information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Proceed with the establishment of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines support and referral centre for attending to survivors of violence
Continue implementing the provision of psychological, socioeconomic and empowerment services to victims of domestic violence, including cash transfers to victims and survivors
Increase availability of shelters for victims of sexual and gender-based violence, and train law enforcement to apply a victim-centred approach to sexual and gender-based violence casework

blocks.summary: Strengthen the response to violence against women
blocks.rationale: A 2024 GBV task force, the Domestic Violence Act 2015 and anti-violence campaigns exist; underreporting and limited victim support persist.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 51 — United Nations subregional team: "limited resources for victim support services"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/3), para. 42 — ICAAD: "Gender Affairs undertook antiviolence campaigns in schools, clinics and communities"

recommendations.text: Strengthen the current system to combat domestic violence, as well as the support for victims
Strengthen measures to address violence against women and girls
Continue its efforts to prevent discrimination, violence against women and domestic violence, promote women’s rights and support gender equality

blocks.summary: Retention of pregnant students and inclusive education
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no specific information on measures on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Consider the development and implementation of measures which allow the inclusion of persons with disabilities and combat discrimination against children with disabilities

themes.theme: Economic & political crisis, natural disasters or other emergencies

blocks.summary: Protect the population in emergencies
blocks.rationale: The State, with UNICEF, expanded social protection and food support after the 2021 La Soufrière eruption.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/VCT/2), para. 31 — Special Rapporteur on environment: "programmes such as the Love Box, whereby the Government purchased food from farmers needing markets, then donated the food to families displaced for months by the volcanic eruption"

recommendations.text: Continue efforts to ensure the well-being of its population, in particular women, children and persons with disabilities, in the implementation of rebuilding strategies following the damage caused by the volcanic eruption

blocks.summary: Accessibility of public buildings and transport
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Increase accessibility to public buildings and transportation to allow the inclusion of all persons with disabilities

blocks.summary: Create appropriate legislative and institutional conditions
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Continue its efforts to create appropriate conditions and a legislative or institutional mechanism for vulnerable groups of women and children, and persons with disabilities

blocks.summary: Access of migrants to services and decriminalisation of irregular entry
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Take steps to enhance the access of migrants, including those in irregular situations, to judicial and other remedies available to them in cases where their rights had been violated

Decriminalize irregular entry and ensure that the minimum guarantees enshrined in the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families are respected
Consider revising its immigration laws, including by decriminalizing irregular entry and adjusting terminology on migrant children and persons with disabilities (Brazil).
